key_insight: Understanding a scene requires more than recognizing what is currently visible: it requires tracking a world that persists beyond the camera view. This paper probes whether visual foundation models provide representations that support this spatial state; the supplied abstract does not report findings.
problem_solved: Assessing whether visual foundation models can support persistent spatial understanding as an observer moves, rather than only recognizing individual images.
method: Probe visual foundation model representations for capabilities needed to maintain a spatial state.
Organize the investigation into four capability levels; the supplied abstract identifies spatial structure, object persistence, and predictive spatial update before cutting off.
Examine spatial understanding in the context of partial visibility, self-motion, and action.
impact: The study targets capabilities relevant to navigation, robotics, and embodied AI. Its framing helps practitioners distinguish image recognition from the spatial representations needed to track unseen surroundings.

paper_title: Probing Spatial State Representations in Visual Foundation Models
paper_authors: Baiqiao Yin, Zhongang Cai, Ruisi Wang, Qiwei Liang, Lei Yang
